related_questions.question: Is there a debt relief program for healthcare workers?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, there are several debt relief programs specifically designed for healthcare workers. These programs can help reduce or eliminate student loan debt for eligible individuals who work in designated fields or locations. Popular options include the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program and various loan repayment programs offered by the National Health Service Corps (NHSC) and the Nurse Corps.

list.snippet: PSLF forgives the remaining balance of eligible federal student loans after 120 qualifying monthly payments while working full-time for a qualifying employer (government or non-profit).
Qualifying employers include government agencies, non-profit hospitals, and certain other non-profit organizations.
Payments must be made under an income-driven repayment plan (such as PAYE, REPAYE, IBR, etc.).

list.title: National Health Service Corps (NHSC) Loan Repayment Program:
list.snippet: Offers loan repayment for clinicians (doctors, dentists, etc.) who work in Health Professional Shortage Areas (HPSAs) for a specified period (usually 2 years).

list.title: Nurse Corps Loan Repayment Program:
list.snippet: For registered nurses (RNs), advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs), and nurse faculty, this program repays a portion of their student loans in exchange for service in eligible facilities with a shortage of nurses.

list.title: Indian Health Service (IHS) Loan Repayment Program:
list.snippet: Repays student loans for eligible health professionals who work in Indian Health Service facilities.

list.title: National Institutes of Health (NIH) Loan Repayment Programs:
list.snippet: Offers loan repayment to health professionals engaged in research.
Many states and individual healthcare employers also offer their own loan repayment or forgiveness programs to attract and retain healthcare professionals.
You can research programs specific to your state or employer through their websites or by contacting their HR or financial aid departments.

list.title: Eligibility requirements vary.
list.snippet: Carefully review the specific requirements for each program to determine if you qualify.

list.title: Service obligations.
list.snippet: Most loan repayment programs require a service commitment in a specific setting or location (e.g., rural area, underserved community).

list.title: Income-driven repayment plans.
list.snippet: PSLF and some other programs require you to be enrolled in an income-driven repayment plan.

list.title: Tax implications.
list.snippet: Some forms of loan forgiveness may be considered taxable income.

list.title: Consult with a financial advisor.
list.snippet: They can help you understand the different programs and choose the best option for your situation.

list.title: Check with your loan servicer.
list.snippet: Your loan servicer can provide information about your loan types and potential eligibility for forgiveness or repayment programs.

list.title: Explore resources.
list.snippet: Websites like StudentAid.gov, Nurse.org, and the Bureau of Health Workforce offer valuable information about available programs.
